defect_interactions.interaction_type: high-density slip bands blocking dislocation movement
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The high-density slip bands significantly block the movement of dislocations and increase the deformation difficulty, leading to the higher strength of the Cr-containing cold-rolled steel strips; high-density slip bands become the main strengthening factor for the cold-rolled strips, so the yield strength of CR20% + annealed strips does not significantly increase despite κ-carbide precipitation.

interfaces.phase_evolution: After 20% cold rolling the constituent phases remain γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase; further annealing changes the 43.5°–45.0° double peak to a single peak (nearly all ferrite → ordered DO3). Annealing at 600 °C promotes κ-carbide precipitation but does not eliminate the cold-rolling dislocations and slip bands, and has no significant effect on δ-ferrite morphology/volume fraction.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar {111} slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% 6Cr strip; the measured average slip band spacing is 45 ± 13 nm, much smaller than the Cr-free strip, giving a stronger reinforcement effect. These high-density slip bands are retained after the 600 °C/3 h anneal.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: ultimate tensile strength / strength of cold-rolled strips

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by cold-crucible levitation melting of 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite; remelted by induction melting and poured into the rotating copper mold. As-cast steel strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained.
Applied to the as-cast strips before cold rolling.

processing_steps.method: cold rolling (CR) - multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Denoted 'CR20%'. Cold rolling with 20% reduction can eliminate some micropores caused by solidification shrinkage and avoids great influence on the structure of the steel strips.

processing_steps.method: annealing in a tubular vacuum furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The defining step of this sample: the CR20% steel strips were further annealed at 600 °C for 3 h, denoted 'CR20% + annealed'. Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h promotes κ-carbide precipitation without coarsening.

structures.overall_structure: γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite (containing an ordered DO3 phase); constituent phases after 20% cold rolling remain γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase, consistent with the as-cast strips. After further annealing, the 43.5°–45.0° double peak changes into a single peak, indicating that almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase. High-density slip bands (from cold rolling) are retained in the austenite.

unmapped_findings: For the CR20% + annealed state the paper reports only that the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of the CR20% + annealed steel strips do not change significantly compared with the CR20% steel strips (Fig. 9); no separate numeric YS/UTS values are printed for the CR20% + annealed 6Cr strip.

The numeric tensile values quoted in the paper (UTS 1154/1270/1264 MPa for CR20% 0Cr/3Cr/6Cr and elongation ~21%) are given for the CR20% (parent) cold-rolled strips rather than the CR20% + annealed strips; the CR20% 6Cr UTS of 1264 MPa and the Cr-addition strengthening comparison in the properties/performance fields are therefore derived from the parent cold-rolled state, which the paper states does not change significantly upon annealing.

In the CR20% + annealed 0Cr and 3Cr strips the κ-carbides precipitate mainly at dislocation entanglement, whereas in the CR20% + annealed 6Cr strip the κ-carbides are too small to observe in the dark-field image (Fig. 12) because Cr addition expands the solid solubility of Al and C and reduces the driving force for κ-carbide formation.
The highest UTS × TE product of 38.0 GPa % was achieved in the as-cast 6Cr strip (not this CR20% + annealed sample).

The CR20% + annealed 6Cr strip contains γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with an ordered DO3 phase, and the 43.5°–45.0° double peak in the XRD pattern changes to a single peak after annealing, indicating nearly all ferrite transforms to ordered DO3.
